contract: The road user is at an intersection whose traffic a signal head controls, and that head is installed with its faces not covered and shows no valid indication at the observation: there is an intersection region which the road user's footprint overlaps, or which a lane the road user's footprint overlaps runs into at its end, and there is a signal head whose faces are not covered, which governs that intersection region or governs a lane that runs into that intersection region, and which is inoperative - installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication. The concept is a configuration at an instant, read from the road user's region and lane membership, from the intersection a lane runs into, from the travel regions the head controls and from the head's own state. It says nothing about which approach of the junction the head stands over: a head over any approach of that intersection, or over the junction itself, satisfies it, whether or not it is the approach the road user came in on. It says nothing about what any other device at the junction shows, nothing about whether a public authority placed or erected the head, nothing about the direction the road user travels, the movement it makes or how fast it goes, nothing about where the road user must halt, and nothing about whether it has halted. It is not a head whose faces are covered, and not the absence of a head; it is not a head that shows a valid indication, a flashing red or a flashing yellow head being an operating head that does not satisfy it; it is not a stop sign, a yield sign or any other sign; it is not a person directing traffic; it is not the lane a lane leads into; and it is not a judgement that the road user has or lacks the right to proceed. Where the scene does not observe whether an installed uncovered head shows a valid indication, or does not observe the travel regions a head controls, the concept is unknown.

elements.span: there is an intersection region which the road user's footprint overlaps
elements.justification: st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', which is the junction the road user is at; rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk, ...)', which anchors the concept to the junction this road user is at rather than any junction of the scene. st.intersection's exclusion, 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line', does not apply: the concept reads no place of a halt, only the junction region a device controls. rel.occupies has no exclusion clause.

elements.span: or which a lane the road user's footprint overlaps runs into at its end
elements.justification: st.lane is 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', the approach the road user runs in; st.lane_enters is 'the intersection region a lane runs into at its end - the lane is an approach to that intersection', which is how a road user still on its approach is at that intersection. st.lane_enters' exclusions do not apply: the concept does not read 'the lane a lane leads into (st.lane_connectivity)' - it reads the junction the lane runs into; it does not read 'the subject's presence in the intersection (rel.occupies)' through it, which the first disjunct reads on its own; and it does not read 'the region a device governs (dev.governs)' through it, which the governance element reads on its own. st.lane's exclusion, that it is not a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane, does not apply: only membership is read.

elements.span: there is a signal head whose faces are not covered
elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with an 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered', which is exactly an installed head with its vehicular faces uncovered. The atom carries no 'not a stand-in for' clause; the head's indication is not read here, the inoperative element reading it instead.

elements.span: which governs that intersection region or governs a lane that runs into that intersection region
elements.justification: dev.governs is the relation to 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls - a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, centre turn lane, bicycle lane or path, roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder - or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself and of nothing else', which is what it is for a junction's traffic to be controlled by a head; st.lane_enters ties a governed lane to the junction it runs into, so that a head over any approach of this junction counts. dev.governs' exclusion, 'Not a stand-in for: a position - the region a device governs is not where a halt is required', does not apply: the concept reads no stopping place and no distance to the head.

elements.span: and which is inoperative - installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication
elements.justification: dev.inoperative is 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', which is word for word the state the contract names. The atom carries no 'not a stand-in for' clause; it is not read as a dark covered head, since the uncovered attribute is read beside it.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Two roadways meet at a junction; the intersection region, the approach lanes and the roadways all carry a reference point and a boundary, and occupancy is stated for every road user and region pair. A signal head is mounted over the northbound approach: it is installed, its faces are not covered, and it shows no valid indication. The head governs the northbound approach lane, and that lane runs into the intersection region at its end. A car's footprint overlaps that approach lane. The concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, the same mapped regions and the same car in the northbound approach lane, except that the head over that approach shows circular_red: an installed, uncovered head showing a valid indication, so no inoperative head governs that lane or the intersection region, and no other head stands at the junction. The concept fails.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, the same mapped regions, the same uncovered installed head governing the northbound approach lane and the same car overlapping that lane, but the source's capability manifest declares dev.inoperative absent: it never observes whether an installed, uncovered head is showing a valid indication. The concept is unknown.

differs_from.why: The accepted concept takes the same single track formal and reads the same junction structure, but it is satisfied by a stop sign, a yield sign or a point regulatory sign as well as by a signal head and, by its own words, 'says nothing about what the device displays - a dark, covered or inoperative head governs its approach exactly as a lit one does'. This concept is satisfied only by a signal head, and only by one that is installed with its faces uncovered and shows no valid indication (dev.traffic_signal's uncovered attribute and dev.inoperative, neither of which the accepted concept reads); it is also satisfied by a head over another approach of the same junction, which the accepted concept's dismissed divergence records that it is not. The two therefore decide differently at a junction with an operating head and at a junction whose head governs only another approach.

narrowings.span: there is an intersection region which the road user's footprint overlaps, or which a lane the road user's footprint overlaps runs into at its end
narrowings.why: Written as ONE existential over the scene's intersection regions, with the junction bound once and both of the contract's elements — the road user's place and the head's control — conjoined under it, so that "that intersection region" denotes the same region in both. The contract's words leave open whether the head's junction is the road user's; the sentence binds them by the demonstrative ("which governs THAT intersection region"), and the single binder is what makes a road user at one junction and an inoperative head at another junction of the same scene fail the concept. The two limbs of the element are joined by an inclusive `.or`: a footprint that overlaps both the junction and a lane running into it satisfies the element by either limb, the contract stating no exclusive choice. The lane limb binds a lane variable of its own, anchored to the formal by `rel_occupies u l`.

narrowings.span: which governs that intersection region or governs a lane that runs into that intersection region
narrowings.why: Inclusive `.or`, and the governed lane is a SECOND bound lane variable (`lg`), never the lane the road user's footprint overlaps. The contract leaves open which approach the head stands over and then settles it: "a head over any approach of that intersection, or over the junction itself, satisfies it, whether or not it is the approach the road user came in on". Writing the governed lane as the road user's own lane would be the narrower reading the contract expressly rejects, so the two lanes are bound separately and are tied to each other only through the junction they both run into. A head that governs both the junction and an approach satisfies the element by either limb.

narrowings.span: there is a signal head whose faces are not covered
narrowings.why: The head's kind is the quantifier's test — `existsDevice (.lit "traffic_signal")`, which reads the dev.traffic_signal atom — and the atom's uncovered attribute is a conjunct beside it, `dev_traffic_signal_uncovered d`, rather than part of the range quantified over. Nothing of the indication the head displays is read here, the inoperative element reading it instead. A head the source sees to be covered makes the conjunction false (not the absence of a head, which makes the existential false as well); a head whose cover the source does not report leaves the existential unknown, which is what the three-valued atoms give and not a choice of this file's.

narrowings.span: and which is inoperative - installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication
narrowings.why: `dev_inoperative d` alone, of the same head as the other two conjuncts, so one head is installed, uncovered, controlling and showing no valid indication; dev_traffic_signal_shows is nowhere in the file. A head showing circular red, a flashing red or a flashing yellow therefore fails the concept through the source's own reading of dev.inoperative rather than through a list of indication spellings, which is what the contract's "a flashing red or a flashing yellow head being an operating head that does not satisfy it" asks for, and what keeps a dark covered head out of the concept, the uncovered attribute being read beside it.

narrowings.span: The concept is a configuration at an instant
narrowings.why: Nothing of the body looks before or after the observation — no window, no rising edge, no `since`, no `always` — and no class, position, heading, speed, movement, stop line, marking or other device is read, so the concept decides the configuration at the instant alone. No `definedWhen` guard is written: the contract names exactly two unknown sources (the head's valid indication, the travel regions a head controls) and both are the plain unknowns of the atoms that read them, while a head the source sees to be uncovered, controlling and operating makes the existential false rather than unknown. No guard that the scene carry lanes is written either: at a junction a source maps without lanes the second limb of each element is false of every region and the concept is decided by the junction region alone.
